newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Bullish dlr/mark eyes further gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Bullish dlr/mark eyes further gains.

text.p: The dollar/mark breakout above the top of a three-day triangle points to fresh dollar gains next week, chartists said on Friday.
At 1740 EDT/2140 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.7070/80 marks, up from 1.7010/20 at the open, and right at the top of a triangle formed over the past three sessions.
The dollar topped out in the 1.7067- to 1.7074-mark area Tuesday to Thursday and set a day high of 1.71 on Friday.
However, technicians stressed one major factor of uncertainty for the charts is the extent of the market reaction to the French general elections on Sunday.
Traders said a defeat of the center-right majority that supports a strict adherence to the Maastricht Treaty criteria would unleash volatility on the European crosses.
"Mark/Paris does deserve attention. If we break 3.3835 French francs, we're going to the moon," predicted analyst Ben Morden at the consultancy firm I.D.E.A.
At 1740 EDT/2140 GMT, the mark traded at 3.3820/22 French francs, a 50-percent retracement of a 3.4015 to 3.3618 move.
Mark/Paris may be key for dollar/mark which is eyeing strong resistance at 1.7120 -- the 62-percent retracement from 1.7389, the high on April 28, to 1.6680, the low on May 12.
Mark/Paris could determine the fate of dollar/mark, with 1.7210 an important level on the way to "revisiting 1.7389, the top of the next range," Morden said.
In contrast, dollar/yen remained confined to a narrow range, closing at 116.20/30 versus 116.40/45 at the open and vs. 116.25/35 at the prior close.

"There is no clear signal on dollar/yen," Morden said, who saw the possibility of a slow grind higher to "117.00 the figure and even 117.85, the 38-percent retracement between 111.88, the low on May 20, and 127.47, the May 1 high."
"Mark/yen will also play a role here," Morden noted.
Mark/yen slipped from a day high of 68.68 to 68.03/06 at the close, just above support at 67.90, a double-bottom.
Analysts said the erosion of mark/yen on Friday reflected global concern about the German and other European currencies.

Mark/Swiss was another cross betraying concern about the European Monetary Union, as the German unit retreated from 0.8387, Wednesday's high, to 0.8290, threatening to test important supports at 0.8260 and then 0.8220.
Sterling/mark was a similar example. The move from a low of 2.7512 on Monday to a high of 2.8015 on Friday, setting the stage for an attack on key resistance at 2.8055.
The dollar suffered somewhat of the strength of both sterling and the Swiss franc vs. the other Europeans. Strong resistances await cable at $1.6430 and dollar/Swiss at 1.4170.
